name: Sri Gnana Saraswati Temple, Basara
deity: The Goddess Saraswati as Gnana Saraswati, giver of learning, with Lakshmi and Kali
tradition: Shaktism, the worship of Saraswati, Devi of learning
period: A rare Saraswati shrine on the Godavari, sought for the child's first lesson (Aksharabhyasam)
summary: On the Godavari at Basara, Saraswati is worshipped as Gnana Saraswati, giver of knowledge — one of the few great Saraswati temples in India, where children are brought for Aksharabhyasam, their first writing of letters.

sections.history: Basara stands on the banks of the Godavari in Telangana, home to one of India's rare temples to Saraswati, the goddess of learning, here called Gnana Saraswati. Tradition ties the place to the sage Vyasa; the very name Basara is said to derive from Vyasara, the abode of Vyasa.
sections.architecture: The temple sits by the river in the South Indian manner, its sanctum holding the goddess Saraswati, with shrines to Lakshmi and Kali nearby, so that the three great goddesses are honoured together. The riverside ghats are part of the pilgrimage.
sections.legends: It is said that Vyasa, after the great war, came here seeking peace and made three handfuls of sand into the images of Saraswati, Lakshmi, and Kali — knowledge, wealth, and power. From his penance the place took its name, and the goddess of learning made it her home.
sections.festivals: Vasant Panchami and the Navaratri days are the great festivals of the goddess of learning. Through the year families arrive for the Aksharabhyasam, when a child first traces letters in the goddess's presence to begin its education.
sections.experience: Basara is above all a temple of beginnings — of children brought to write their first letters before Saraswati — a quiet, riverside pilgrimage bound to the hope of learning and wisdom.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening worship and a midday break; Vasant Panchami is busiest, and Aksharabhyasam is performed through the day. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Basara lies on the Godavari in Nirmal district of Telangana, near the Maharashtra border; it has its own railway station on the Secunderabad–Manmad line and is reached by road from Nizamabad.
